messages:
Joel: FYI CI microbench failed on PR #21777 — batcher/kernel path. Seeing a tail latency spike in batch_wait_time and an unexpected kv-cache hit drop.
Alex: repro locally?
Joel: not yet fully reprod locally; CI microbench shows +3.6% p99 for batch_wait_time and ~6% kv-hit rate drop on 2x runs. Attached excerpt from runner: 
```
microbench: batch_wait_time p50: 1.8ms p95: 12.3ms p99: 32.1ms (baseline p99 30.9ms)
kvcache: hit_rate: 0.842 -> 0.792
kernel: selected=quant_fast_v2 (fallback path taken more often)
```
Ravi: hmm kernel selector change landed in the same PR? I recall a small tiebreaker tweak in kernel_autoselect.cc — commit 9b7d2ea. Bisecting now.
Maria: CI Bot posted the failure summary too. If bisect points to kernel_autoselect, we might need a targeted revert or hotfix. Can't block the deploy longer than a day.
CI Bot: PR #21777 — microbench/coldpath failed (threshold exceeded). Logs: https://ci.internal/reports/21777/bench/attach
Sam: quick flamegraph from the CI artifact shows extra time in memcpy + scheduler stall right before batch flush. Looks like more fanout into worker threads: link https://s3.internal/ci/21777/flamegraph.svg
Alex: Could be batching latch contention — the new tiebreaker nudges some seqlen distributions toward fanout-heavy kernels, increasing wakeups. Any profiling of lock hold times?
Joel: I ran a short perf on canary with the PR and saw batcher::enqueue hold distribution shift: median 120ns -> 350ns, 99th 1.2us -> 2.8us. Also saw more calls to kernel_dispatcher::probe() during warmup.
Ravi: bisect nailed it: 9b7d2ea -> kernel_autoselect: added cpu-cost tiebreaker. Reverting that commit locally removes the p99 delta in our smoke runs.
Maria: please open an urgent revert PR and mark as rollout-blocker. Lina can you open the revert and trigger CI?
Lina: opening revert PR now (PR #21782) with description: revert kernel_autoselect tiebreaker commit 9b7d2ea. Kicking off CI. 
Lina: CI started — will post results.
CI Bot: PR #21782 queued for CI. Will update on pass/fail.
Joel: thanks. If revert passes we'll ship hotfix and re-evaluate kernel tiebreaker more conservatively (maybe weight by seqlen histogram instead of raw cpu-cost).
Sam: also worth adding a microbench that simulates warmup fanout patterns to catch this in future thresholds.
Alex: agree. Add test + a telemetry flag to sample kernel selection during shadow rollouts.
Maria: plan: hold master rollouts until revert is merged and canary validated. I'll post a rollout hold note. :no_entry_sign:
Joel: will follow up with a small proposal to make the selector less eager and include hysteresis.
__notes: Generated Slack thread about CI microbenchmark failure, bisect to kernel selector change, revert PR, and next steps. All fields are strings or list of strings as required.
